label: The f″ mode's first real payoff: ca-02-02 (The Second-Derivative Test). The authored reveal shows the test FAILING — x⁴, −x⁴, x³ all have f′(0)=0 and f″(0)=0 with three different verdicts. Inserted after it is the complement the lesson never had: the test WORKING, on x³−3x, where f″=6x is −6 at one critical point and +6 at the other. Same test, opposite signs, opposite verdicts — and the learner drags across the inflection at x=0 to watch the sign flip. Reveal keeps its teaching; the lab supplies the doing.

step.body: That reveal showed the test's blind spot. Now watch it work — on a curve where f″ is nowhere near zero at the points that matter.

predict.prompt: This is f(x) = x³ − 3x. Its tangent goes flat in two places. Do you expect the second-derivative test to return the same verdict at both?

options.label: No — one is a max, the other a min
No — f″ will be 0 at both, like the three curves above

predict.reveal: Drag across both and watch the third pane: f″ = 6x, so it reads −6 at the left flat point and +6 at the right. One test, opposite signs, opposite verdicts.

widget.prompt: Drag to the flat point that the second-derivative test calls a MAXIMUM — the one where the bend is downward.
widget.successFeedback: f′(−1) = 0 and f″(−1) = −6. Flat tangent, bending downward — the test returns MAXIMUM in a single step, and the top pane shows the peak at (−1, 2). That is the whole point: when f″ is not zero it decides immediately. The three curves above were the case where it cannot.
widget.lowFeedback: Not there yet — f′ is still above zero here, so the curve is still climbing toward the peak. The f″ pane is already negative, so the bend is the right one; keep going right until f′ reaches zero.
widget.highFeedback: You have gone past the maximum — come back left. Watch the f″ pane on the way: to the right of x = 0 it is positive, and the flat point over there is the MINIMUM. The test wants the flat point where the bend is downward.

refusals.title: Rolle's Theorem (curve-analysis)
refusals.why: LEDGER CORRECTION, NOT A NEW REFUSAL. The S205B patch recorded this id against reasoning about concavity, f″ and inflection — but ca-03-01 is Rolle's Theorem. The concavity lesson is ca-02-01 and the f″-test lesson is ca-02-02 (this patch's target). The cited engine gap was real and is now closed; the lesson id attached to it was wrong. Rolle's Theorem itself remains unconverted for a different and still-standing reason: its steppedReveal argues the EXISTENCE claim (equal endpoint heights force a flat tangent somewhere between), and derivativeTrace has no way to let a learner vary the endpoints — fn is a fixed four-item enum (schema.ts:3136) with no interval controls, so the learner cannot test the hypothesis by breaking it. Needs an engine with a movable interval; recorded as an engine gap.

refusals.title: Concavity and the Second Derivative (curve-analysis)
refusals.why: Already Tier A (total 32) on a fresh tier scan, and its interactive step is a signChart, not a steppedReveal — it is not on the wall and not eligible for conversion.
